script: I begged theaters for intermissions—my request got brutally rejected.. If a movie is over three hours long, I think it should have a 10‑minute intermission. Picture this: you're in the theater, popcorn stuck to your fingers, eyes glued to the screen, and the clock ticking. You're like, "Do I keep sitting or do I just get up and ruin the vibe?" I am saying, "No jerks here, just take a breather." You get to hit the restroom—no one's going to miss the cliffhanger. You can stretch, grab a refill, maybe even hit the snack aisle for a second round of nachos. Some people claim an intermission messes with the pacing. They're like, "It'll break the flow." But honestly, watching the same person pop in and out every 15 minutes is way more annoying. So I am like, "Why not give us a quick reset?" It's a tiny price for a whole lot more comfort. No more cramped legs, no more cramping. Just a clean break that keeps the story tight and the audience happy.
